title: I just released Ironfields, a single-player RTS built with Godot and AI assistance!
author: Hot_Tell2552
selftext:
Hi everyone!

I just released Ironfields, my single-player RTS, on Steam!

I developed the game in Godot with the help of AI tools. I handled the game design, mechanics, balancing, testing, and overall direction, while AI assisted me with programming, voiceovers, translations, and parts of the map creation.

The game is inspired by older RTS titles like State of War, but plays differently from most traditional RTS games.

There's no base building. Instead, buildings are scattered across the map, each providing different bonuses. Capturing and holding them is the key to winning. The game has a slower, more tactical pace, where each mission requires a different approach.

The full campaign features 30 missions of varying difficulty.

There's also a map editor that lets players create their own layouts, import custom maps from images, and share their creations through Steam Workshop.

The demo is still available if you'd like to try it first.

**Steam:** [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4700280/Ironfields/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4700280/Ironfields/)

Happy to answer any questions about the game or my experience developing it with AI assistance!

comments.author: WWEtrump
comments.body: congrats on shipping an rts, that's the hard genre. no base building and capturing buildings to hold the map is such a different feel from the usual. i'm solo on a toy brick rts that's still waiting on steamworks approval, so honestly curious: what got your first wishlists and players, reddit posts or something else?

replies.author: Hot_Tell2552
replies.body:
Thanks! :)

My first bigger spike in wishlists came when I released the trailer and sent it to GameTrailers. It also ended up on IGN China's channel, which brought in most of my wishlists at that time.

The second big spike came when Perafilozof featured Ironfields in one of his RTS news and updates videos. That helped quite a lot!

The third boost came when I released the demo, but the biggest growth happened during Steam Next Fest. In the last 15 days before release, my wishlists practically doubled, going from around 1,350 to over 2,600.

So for me, coverage from YouTube channels and Steam Next Fest made the biggest difference. Reddit posts helped get some attention too, but they weren't the main source of wishlists.

Good luck with your RTS and getting through Steamworks approval! :)

comments.author: Vindelator
comments.body: How were the art assets made?

replies.author: Hot_Tell2552
replies.body:
I made the 3D models manually. I actually tried using AI for modeling at first, but couldn't get the results I wanted. I was aiming for a low-poly style, with models ranging from around 600 to 2,000 polygons.

For the maps, I designed the layouts myself and then used AI to generate the final images based on my references, making sure the different parts fit together with clean transitions.

I worked on the models about six months ago, though, so maybe AI could do a better job today. The progress has been pretty crazy!

replies.author: Vindelator
replies.body:
Thanks. I've got so much to learn. 

This reminds me a lot of the old Total Annihilation games from when I was a kid. Those games never stopped being fun either. Planetary Annihilation now is pretty cool.
